header.name: Saturn V
header.description: Saturn V — NASA's Apollo Moon launcher, 1967–1973. CPACS model of the three-stage civil launch vehicle flown by NASA on the Apollo and Skylab missions. Built entirely from published, unrestricted documentation (see the source list in the file header) as a demonstration dataset for the CPACS systems, fuelTanks and decks definitions.

model.name: Saturn V
model.description: NASA's Apollo Moon launcher, 1967–1973. Civil three-stage expendable launch vehicle (S-IC / S-II / S-IVB) with Apollo spacecraft and launch escape system.

duct.name: S-IC LOX Tunnel f1_1
duct.description: Tunnel carrying the oxidizer suction line of an outboard F-1 engine through the RP-1 fuel tank. Coaxial with the upstream leg of loxSuctionLine_dn430_inclined, inner diameter 26 in. The duct runs from station 757 down to station 242 and therefore protrudes beyond both fuel tank bulkheads, so that the cutouts are fully open at either end.

duct.name: S-IC Thrust Structure Shell Cut
duct.description: Interior cutting body of the S-IC thrust structure (vehicle stations 112 to 365). Cutting body for the stage shell. It is the fuselage outer mould line offset inward by a radial wall thickness of 50.8 mm (2 in), which is the order of the skin-stringer structural depth of the Saturn V shell sections. The body overshoots each fuselage end face by 200 mm so that the end caps of the fuselage solid are cut into annuli and no coplanar faces meet in the Boolean operation.

ductAssembly.name: S-IC LOX Tunnel Assembly
ductAssembly.description: Cuts the five oxidizer suction line tunnels into the RP-1 fuel tank vessel. excludeObjectUIDs is an opt-out list, so the thrust structure and the intertank section, which the tunnels overshoot into, are listed here to keep them uncut.

ductAssembly.name: S-IC Shell Cut Assembly
ductAssembly.description: Cuts the S-IC shell sections open so that only the ring structure of the given wall thickness remains. excludeObjectUIDs is an opt-out list: the RP-1 and LOX tanks are listed because their bulkheads reach into the thrust structure, the intertank and the forward skirt and must stay intact, and the S-II interstage skirt is listed because the forward cutting body overshoots into it; it is cut by s-ii_shellCutAssembly instead.

ductAssembly.name: S-II Shell Cut Assembly
ductAssembly.description: Cuts the S-II shell sections open. The LOX and LH2 tanks are excluded because they fill the stage over its full diameter, the S-IC forward skirt and the S-IVB aft interstage assembly because the cutting bodies overshoot into them.

ductAssembly.name: S-IVB Shell Cut Assembly
ductAssembly.description: Cuts the S-IVB shell sections and the instrument unit open. The LH2 and LOX tanks are excluded because the S-IVB tank outer diameter equals the skirt outer diameter, the S-II forward skirt and the LM adapter because the cutting bodies overshoot into them.

ductAssembly.name: SLA Shell Cut Assembly
ductAssembly.description: Cuts the conical spacecraft/lunar module adapter open, which is the bay the lunar module is stowed in. The instrument unit is excluded because the aft overshoot reaches into it; it is cut by s-ivb_shellCutAssembly instead. The service and command modules are excluded so that the spacecraft stays closed.

fuselage.name: S-IC Thrust Structure
fuselage.description: Aft structural section of the S-IC first stage supporting the engine cluster and lower tank interfaces. Positioning root of the vehicle; its aft face is at vehicle station 112.0 in (2.8448 m), stations increasing forward from the theoretical datum 100 in below the F-1 gimbal plane [1]. The S-IC diameter is 396 in [1].

fuselage.name: Service Module
fuselage.description: Service Module (SM) of the Apollo spacecraft. Begins at vehicle station 3593.5 (370.94 in above the theoretical datum at STA 3222.56) [3]. The forward face, derived from this dataset's own section geometry rather than an independent source, is at approximately STA 3770.7 (548.1 in above STA 3222.56); this value should be verified against a primary source before use.

enginePylon.name: S-IC Engine Shroud 1
enginePylon.description: Thin-walled half-cone engine shroud enclosing the outboard side of F-1 engine 1, per MSFC drawing 10M04564 (SHROUD, 4 PLACES). Aft radius 100.03 in (2.5408 m), cone angle 15 deg, wall thickness 0.05 m. Modelled as an enginePylon because CPACS offers no parametric component for aerodynamic fairings; the shell is obtained from an open C-shaped wing airfoil instead of a closed profile.

fuelTank.name: S-IC RP-1 Tank
fuelTank.description: Propellant tank of the S-IC first stage storing RP-1 fuel. The cylindrical part spans vehicle stations 365 to 602 (253 in and 490 in above the theoretical datum at STA 112) [2]. The total tank length is 517 in [1]; therefore each dome measures 140 in, consistent with direct measurement in [1]. The tank diameter is 396 in [1]. The lowest point of the cylinder is at STA 225 (113 in above the theoretical datum at STA 112) [1]; STA 112 itself coincides with the top of the heat shield and the aft face of s-ic_thrustStructure.

vessel.name: S-IC RP-1 Tank Vessel

fuelTank.name: S-IC LOX Tank
fuelTank.description: Propellant tank of the S-IC first stage storing liquid oxygen as oxidizer. The cylindrical part spans vehicle stations 912 to 1401 (800 in and 1289 in above the theoretical datum at STA 112) [2]. The total tank length is 769 in [1]; therefore each dome measures 140 in.

vessel.name: S-IC LOX Tank Vessel
vessel.description: Pressure vessel with ellipsodial bulkheads representing the liquid-oxygen tank volume of the S-IC stage.

fuelTank.name: S-II LOX Tank
fuelTank.description: Propellant tank of the S-II second stage storing liquid oxygen as oxidizer. The tank consists of ellipsoidal fore and aft halves joined at a 15 in bolting ring, which also carries the attachment of the aft skirt and of the LH2 cylinder [9]; it therefore has no barrel of its own beyond that ring. The forward half is the common bulkhead shared with the s-ii_lh2 tank and protrudes forward into the LH2 volume [9]. Tank diameter 396 in (10.0584 m); dome depth 128.19 in, i.e. halfAxisFraction = 0.647419. Generated by generate_s_ii_tanks.py.

vessel.name: S-II LOX Tank Vessel
vessel.description: Pressure vessel representing the liquid-oxygen tank volume of the S-II stage. Both closures are convex outwards, so unlike the LH2 tank this vessel maps onto the parametric domeType branch and is described by cylinderRadius, cylinderLength and domeType/ellipsoid. The sources describe the bulkheads as "modified ellipsoidal" [9] and the gores as carrying a toroidal/elliptical/conical compound contour [4]; the pure ellipsoid used here is therefore an approximation, chosen so that the tank stays parametric. The aft sections of the s-ii_lh2 vessel are sampled from this same ellipsoid so that the common bulkhead is a single coincident surface. cylinderLength is the 15 in bolting ring [9]. The bolting ring is placed entirely aft of the LOX tank equator at STA 1848; no source states on which side of that station it sits.

fuelTank.name: S-II LH2 Tank
fuelTank.description: Propellant tank of the S-II second stage storing liquid hydrogen as fuel. The cylindrical section begins at the LOX tank equator, STA 1848 (307 in above the theoretical datum at STA 1541) [2,3]; the barrel is closed forward by an ellipsoidal bulkhead and aft by the common bulkhead shared with the S-II LOX tank [3,4]. Both bulkheads are described in the primary sources as "modified ellipsoidal" and are convex in the forward direction, i.e. the forward bulkhead bulges out of the tank while the common bulkhead protrudes back into the LH2 volume [9]. Tank diameter 396 in (10.0584 m); forward bulkhead depth 138.27 in, common bulkhead depth 128.19 in, both measured from the respective Y-ring / bolting-ring tangent plane to the apex. Generated by generate_s_ii_tanks.py.

vessel.name: S-II LH2 Tank Vessel
vessel.description: Pressure vessel representing the liquid-hydrogen tank volume of the S-II stage. The vessel is described by explicit sections and segments rather than by the parametric domeType branch, because the aft closure is a common bulkhead shared with the S-II LOX tank and is convex forward, i.e. re-entrant into the LH2 volume, and because the forward bulkhead carries the "modified ellipsoidal" compound contour documented for the S-II gores [4], which no single domeType reproduces. Aft closure: a pure ellipsoid of depth 3.2560 m, sampled from exactly the contour that the s-ii_lox vessel generates from domeType/ellipsoid with halfAxisFraction = 0.647419, so that the two tanks share a coincident surface. Forward closure: four tangent-continuous pieces of revolution, in this order from the equator to the apex, a toroidal knuckle tangent to the cylindrical barrel, an elliptical crown, a conical band, and a spherical cap closing the central circular "dollar" plate. Sections are placed on the three piece boundaries so that the curvature discontinuities coincide with segment ends; the remaining sections sample the knuckle and the crown at fixed meridian angles. The ordering of the three gore curves is an interpretation of [4], which names them without giving a sequence; the knuckle extent and the width of the conical band are modelling choices, as no source gives dish, knuckle or cone dimensions for the S-II bulkheads. The bulkhead depths are taken from the station-based stack-up. Relative to a pure ellipsoid of equal height the forward bulkhead encloses -1.3 % volume and its meridian deviates by at most 29 mm.

fuelTank.name: S-IVB LH2 Tank
fuelTank.description: Propellant tank of the S-IVB third stage storing liquid hydrogen as fuel. Modelled as the complete welded propellant tank: barrel from STA 2832.00 to 3100.56, closed by two outward convex ellipsoidal domes of 122 in depth, apexes at STA 2710.00 and 3222.56 [8]. The forward apex coincides with the forward skirt / Instrument Unit interface at STA 3222.56; the dome fills the forward skirt exactly. s-ivb_lox is nested inside this envelope and shares its aft dome, so this vessel encloses 13249 cu ft rather than the 10418 cu ft of the LH2 compartment [5]; the compartment is the difference between the two.

vessel.name: S-IVB LH2 Tank Vessel
vessel.description: Pressure vessel representing the welded propellant tank of the S-IVB stage. It is the outer envelope; s-ivb_lox_vessel sits inside it.

fuelTank.name: S-IVB LOX Tank
fuelTank.description: Propellant tank of the S-IVB third stage storing liquid oxygen as oxidizer. Lens formed by the aft dome of the surrounding tank and the common bulkhead, welded together at one attach ring at STA 2779.63 and inserted into the barrel as a closed unit [8, Fig. 28]. The ring lies on the aft dome, so its radius 117.41 in follows from its station; the station itself is solved from the documented 2830 cu ft [5]. The bulkhead is convex forward, of the same 0.9385 proportion, with its apex at STA 2889.82. The two closures meet at a kink -- the aft dome arrives at 64.58 deg meridian angle, the bulkhead leaves at 90 deg -- so the vessel is described by sections and segments; no domeType can express two dissimilar closures.

vessel.name: S-IVB LOX Tank Vessel
vessel.description: Pressure vessel representing the liquid-oxygen tank volume of the S-IVB stage. Its aft closure is geometrically identical to the aft dome of s-ivb_lh2_vessel, which it shares as a physical part.

pipe.name: Fuel Suction Line DN300, 45.1 deg Elbow (Outboard)
pipe.description: Two-piece oxidizer-side RP-1 suction line of an outboard engine, with a single elbow. Local origin at the inlet flange, local +z is the axis of the downstream leg, the elbow deflects toward local +x. Elbow angle 45.1440 deg, bend radius 0.4500 m. Geometry from [1]: the engine side inlets sit beside the oxidizer suction line inlet, their centres offset 23.08 in to either side of it (Section A-A); the elbow sits at station 187.7; the tank outlet fittings sit on the aft RP-1 bulkhead on a circle of radius 84.056 in (Section D-D), the outboard engine fittings offset about 12 deg and the centre engine fittings about 34 deg to either side of the engine position line.

pipe.name: Fuel Suction Line DN300, 31.8 deg Elbow (Inboard)
pipe.description: RP-1 suction line of the centre engine, with a single elbow. Local origin at the inlet flange, local +z is the axis of the downstream leg, the elbow deflects toward local +x. Elbow angle 31.7736 deg, bend radius 0.4500 m. Geometry from [1]: the engine side inlets sit beside the oxidizer suction line inlet, their centres offset 23.08 in to either side of it (Section A-A); the elbow sits at station 187.7; the tank outlet fittings sit on the aft RP-1 bulkhead on a circle of radius 84.056 in (Section D-D), the outboard engine fittings offset about 12 deg and the centre engine fittings about 34 deg to either side of the engine position line.

pipe.name: LOX Suction Line 20 in, Single Elbow (Outboard)
pipe.description: Oxidizer suction line of an outboard engine, running from the tank aft bulkhead to the engine inlet with a single elbow at a ball joint. Local origin at the inlet flange, local +z is the axis of the downstream leg, the elbow deflects toward local +x. The inlet sits on the aft LOX bulkhead at radius 61.22 in [1], the ball joint at station 210.52 and radius 132.7 in [1], the outlet at station 112.0. The ball joint is not a true sphere; the intermediate sections are scaled from a sphere of 31 in diameter measured in [1].

pipe.name: LOX Suction Line 20 in, Single Elbow (Inboard)
pipe.description: Oxidizer suction line of the centre engine, also used as a third tank fill path, with a single elbow at a ball joint. Local origin at the inlet flange, local +z is the axis of the downstream leg, the elbow deflects toward local +x. The inlet sits on the apex of the aft LOX bulkhead at station 772.0 [1], the ball joint at station 210.52 [1], the outlet at station 112.0. The downstream leg is parallel to the vehicle axis and offset 49.5 in from the engine axis, the same offset that the outboard lines show between engine axis and inlet fitting [1]. The ball joint is not a true sphere; the intermediate sections are scaled from a sphere of 31 in diameter measured in [1].
